source.title: Open Problems in Partial Differential Equations Arising from Fluid Dynamics

accepted.question_text: For the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations for a polytropic gas, is the Cauchy problem globally well posed in time for entropy weak solutions with large initial data in the space BV of functions of bounded total variation? In particular, can one obtain global existence, uniqueness, and physically meaningful entropy admissibility for large-BV data in the natural shock-wave setting?

evidence.quote: Global (in time) well-posedness of entropy weak solutions to the Cauchy problems of the one-dimensional Euler equations for polytropic gas dynamics in the space of functions with bounded total variations (which is BV space).

accepted.question_text: Let a weak solution of the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations for a polytropic fluid arise as a vanishing-viscosity limit of the corresponding compressible Navier-Stokes equations as viscosity and heat conductivity go to zero. Must that limit be the unique entropy-admissible weak solution of the Euler Cauchy problem, or at least the unique weak solution obtainable as such a zero-dissipation limit?

evidence.quote: Uniqueness of the vanishing viscosity limits. Consider a weak solution to the one-dimensional Euler equations for polytropic fluids, which is a limit (in appropriate topology) of solutions of the corresponding Navier-Stokes equations as the dissipation parameters (viscosity and heat conduction coefficients) tend to zero.

Show that such a solution is the unique weak solution to the Cauchy problem for the Euler equations under appropriate entropy conditions. A less ambitious problem is to prove that such a solution is unique among the class of weak solutions which can be obtained as limit of solutions to the corresponding Navier-Stokes equations

accepted.question_text: For the full compressible Euler equations of a polytropic fluid with spatially periodic boundary conditions, do global-in-time spatially periodic weak solutions exist, and what is their large-time asymptotic behavior? More specifically, are there examples with piecewise constant periodic initial data that cease to exist in finite time, or examples whose values decay to their average over each period with different rates in time?

evidence.quote: Spatial periodic solutions. In their fundamental work [25], Glimm and Lax obtained the existence and large time asymptotic behavior of spatial periodic solutions to the isentropic Euler equations.

the theory of global (in time) existence and large time asymptotic behavior of spatial periodic solutions to the full Euler equation for polytropic fluids remains completely open. ... Is there example of spatial periodic weak solution for the full Euler equation with piecewise constant periodic initial data which ceases to exist in finite time? Are there examples of special spatial periodic solutions which decay to their average values over each period with different rate of decay in time?

accepted.question_text: Suppose V(x,t) is a BV weak solution of the full compressible Euler equations for a polytropic fluid satisfying the physical entropy condition. What additional local structure must V(x,t) have in physical space beyond merely belonging to BV, and can it be described locally as an appropriate perturbation of a Riemann solution or even as a viscosity solution in the sense of Bressan?
accepted.context_brief: local structure of BV Euler solutions

evidence.quote: Local structures of solutions in BV space. Let V(x,t) ∈ BV be a weak solution to the full Euler equations of polytropic fluids satisfying the physical entropy condition. What are the additional local structures of V(x,t) in the physical space beyond those of a BV functions [26]? Can V(x,t) behave locally as an appropriate perturbation of a Riemann solutions as Glimm solutions do? In particular, can V(x,t) be an viscosity solution in the sense of [8]?

accepted.question_text: For multidimensional compressible Euler equations with generic smooth initial data, smooth solutions can blow up in finite time. Can one characterize the structure of the singularities that form from such smooth data, and in particular determine when genuine shock formation occurs before the development of shell singularities?

evidence.quote: Structures of singularities and formation of shocks. ... However, the nature of singularities in the solutions is not clear except for special cases for which the singularities are shown to be shocks ... It is important to characterize the structures of singularities forming from smooth solutions in terms of initial data. In particular, it is of great interest to determine when shocks form first before the development of shell singularities.

accepted.question_text: For the compressible Euler equations in higher space dimensions, what is the correct well-posedness theory for physically relevant weak solutions? This includes identifying appropriate functional spaces, describing the geometric structure and interactions of generic discontinuities, formulating the right entropy conditions, determining the asymptotic stability of planar shock waves and centered rarefaction waves under non-planar perturbations, and deciding when existence, uniqueness, or compactness of the solution operator should hold.

evidence.quote: The well-posedness of weak solutions. The well-posedness of weak solutions to the compressible Euler equations in higher space dimensions remains to be one of the most challenging open problems for mathematical theory of compressible fluid dynamics.

What are the geometric structures of generic discontinuities in a weak solution? How do the basic linear and nonlinear waves evolve and interact? What are the appropriate entropy conditions? Are the planar shock waves ... and centered rarefactions waves asymptotically stable under non-planary perturbations? What is the appropriate space in which one can obtain either existence (even for short time) or uniqueness of general physically relevant weak solutions? When is the solution operator compact?

accepted.question_text: For the compressible Navier-Stokes equations for viscous polytropic flows with fixed positive viscosity and nonnegative heat conductivity and without exterior forcing, is the Cauchy problem or the initial-boundary-value problem globally well posed for large data? If singularities form in finite or infinite time, can vacuum appear even when the initial data are initially away from vacuum, what are the admissible function spaces for post-singularity weak solutions, and what is the large-time asymptotic behavior of those weak solutions?

evidence.quote: Global (in time) well-posedness of the Cauchy problem or initial-boundary value of problem for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with large data. Consider the Navier Stokes equations for viscous polytropic flows with fixed positive viscosity and nonnegative heat conductivity without exterior forcing.

Is there formation of singularities in finite time (or even in infinite time) for the solutions with large smooth data [39]? Can the vacuum state be formed in finite time even the data are given away from the vacuum? If there exist singularities forming from smooth solutions, can one characterize the structures of the singularity ... ? What are the appropriate spaces to study the weak solutions after formations of singularities? What are the large time asymptotic behavior of the weak solutions?

accepted.question_text: For the multidimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations, are basic nonlinear wave patterns such as planar viscous shock profiles, viscous rarefaction waves, and contact waves nonlinearly stable under generic multidimensional perturbations? Can one also determine the leading-order, or even higher-order, large-time asymptotic ansatz for solutions whose initial data are small perturbations of these wave patterns?

evidence.quote: Large time asymptotic states for the multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations. ... It is of great interest to know whether basic nonlinear wave patterns such as planar viscous shock profiles and viscous rarefaction waves, and contact waves are nonlinearly stable under generic multi-dimensional perturbations. Can one determine the leading order (or even higher order) asymptotic ansatz of a solution to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations when its initial data are small perturbations of these basic wave patterns?

accepted.question_text: In the limit of small viscosity and heat conductivity for compressible flow, are solutions of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations asymptotically equivalent to the corresponding Euler solutions? This includes the zero-dissipation limit near entropy-satisfying shock discontinuities, the more delicate case of contact discontinuity surfaces because of vortex-sheet instability, and the rigorous validity of Prandtl-type boundary layer theory for physically relevant flows with solid boundaries.

evidence.quote: Asymptotic equivalence between Navier-Stokes system and Euler equations for compressible fluid in the limit of small dissipation.

In the case that the underlying Euler flows are piecewise smooth with finitely many entropy satisfying shock discontinuities, it is exported that solutions to the Navier-Stokes equation will converge uniformly to the corresponding solutions to the Euler equations except around thin layers near shock discontinuities in the zero dissipation limit

The case that the solutions to the Euler equation are piecewise smooth containing contact discontinuous surfaces is more subtle due to the instability of vortex sheets ... the well-known boundary layer phenomena occur due to discrepancy of the non-slip boundary conditions for the Navier-Stokes system and the prescribed normal component of the velocity field at the boundaries for the Euler equations ... the well-known Prandtl's laminar boundary layer theory whose validity and rigorous justification are completely open

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations, do smooth solutions of the Cauchy problem break down in finite time? Equivalently, can vorticity stretching and accumulation create a finite-time singularity from smooth initial data, or does global smooth well-posedness persist?

evidence.quote: Well-posedness of the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations. Do smooth solutions to the 3-dimensional incompressible Euler equations break down in finite time?

accepted.question_text: For the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations with vortex-sheet initial data, can one obtain classical weak solutions for general initial vortex sheets rather than only measure-valued solutions, and are such solutions unique? Relatedly, for approximate solutions generated by viscous approximation or vortex methods, can energy concentration occur dynamically even when the initial data are strongly convergent in energy norm, and how are these issues connected to concentration-cancellation phenomena?

evidence.quote: Vortex sheets problem and concentration of energy for 2-dimensional Euler equations. Although 2-dimensional smooth inviscid incompressible flows are very well understood to some extent, yet many important questions involving 2-dimensional singular flows remain to be answered.

It is of fundamental importance both physically and mathematically to know whether such a concentration-cancellation occurs to yield the existence of classical weak solution (in contrast to measure-valued solutions) to 2-D Euler equations with general vortex sheets initial data.

Does the same phenomena occur for general vortex sheets initial data? Does energy-concentration occur at all dynamically for such approximate solutions ... ? ... Finally, the uniqueness of weak solutions to the 2-D Euler equations are wildly open except the case where initial vorticity are bounded in the super-norm [52].

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, does there exist a global smooth solution for arbitrary smooth data? More broadly, what are the asymptotic behaviors of Navier-Stokes solutions as time goes to infinity or as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, do inertial manifolds exist for the two- and three-dimensional equations, is Prandtl boundary-layer theory valid for viscous incompressible flow near boundaries, and what asymptotic forms arise when the limiting Euler solution is singular?

evidence.quote: Regularity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. Although there is no evidence either numerically or physically to support the breaking down of smooth solutions to the 3-D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, yet the global (in time) existence of smooth to the 3-D incompressible Navier-Stokes system is one of the most challenging mathematical problems to be solved.

Other important open problems include: asymptotic behavior of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations either as time approaches infinitely or as Reynold number goes to infinity; do inertial manifolds exist for 2-D or 3-D Navier-Stokes equations [50]? Is Prandtl's boundary layer theory valid for the viscous incompressible fluids in the presence of boundary [43, 46]? What are the asymptotic forms of the solutions to the Navier-Stokes system as the Reynold number goes to infinity in the case of corresponding Euler solutions are singular?

accepted.question_text: For the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation, can one rigorously justify the hydrodynamic limit to the compressible Euler or Navier-Stokes equations in the presence of shocks, contact discontinuities, or physical boundaries, rather than only for smooth flows without boundaries or for special simplified models?

evidence.quote: The rigorous mathematical justification of this fluid-dynamic approximations of Boltzmann solutions poses a challenging open problem in most important cases, in particular, in the case that there are shock discontinuities in the fluid flow and/or in the presence of boundaries.
The hydro-dynamic limit problem in the presence of discontinuities in the fluid flows is completely open for general nonlinear Boltzmann equation except for Broadwell model [72, 76].

accepted.question_text: Can one develop a rigorous theory of shock layers and boundary layers for the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation, including both the construction of matched asymptotic expansions and the convergence analysis needed to justify those asymptotics in the hydrodynamic limit?

evidence.quote: Even a formal asymptotic theory for the shock layer and boundary layer problems has not been achieved.
it is of fundamental importance to understand the fluid dynamic approximation to the nonlinear Boltzmann equation in the presence of shocks and boundaries.

accepted.question_text: For the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation, do there exist global large-amplitude smooth solutions, beyond perturbative or near-equilibrium regimes?

evidence.quote: Other related questions, such as global existence of large amplitude smooth solution to the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation [3], ... are waiting to be attacked too.

accepted.question_text: For renormalized weak solutions of the general nonlinear Boltzmann equation in the sense of DiPerna-Lions, what regularity can be proved, and can one then rigorously derive their hydrodynamic limit toward macroscopic fluid equations?

evidence.quote: Other related questions, such as ... the regularity of the renormalized weak solutions to Boltzmann equations due to Diperna-Lions ([77]) and its hydro-dynamic limit, are waiting to be attacked too.
